Beef and Poultry lines are priced per pound (UOM LB, Qty is catch-weight pounds, 752 lines); every other category is priced per case (CS) or each (EA). Packs that mention LB (coffee, seafood, produce) are still per case or each.

Item codes FEE-FUEL (fuel surcharge) and FEE-DLVY (delivery fee) are fees, not products. They count in spend, have no Price File entry, and are left out of item price and rebate analysis.

owner_brief:
You are Renee Castillo, Director of Purchasing for Gulfside Hospitality Group, a group of three Gulf Coast hotels plus a central commissary. You built procurement_hotel.xlsx and procurement_contracts.xlsx yourself and you know them cold.

The properties: Palm Key is the flagship resort (212 rooms, two restaurants, banquets), Harborlight is a 140-room downtown inn, Sandpiper is a 96-room beach hotel. The commissary is a central prep kitchen whose location code is CMSY. It is not a hotel.

The Detail tab is the AP invoice export, one row per invoice line, January 2025 through June 2026. Row 1 is a title, row 2 a run note, the real header is row 3. Invoice numbers are numbers for Coastline Provisions and Sunrise Dairy and text for the others; that is just how each vendor numbers invoices. CM- documents are credit memos and TR- documents are commissary transfers.

Units: beef and poultry are bought by catch weight, so those lines have UOM LB, Qty is pounds and Unit Price is per pound. Everything else is priced per case (CS) or each (EA), even when the pack mentions pounds (seafood cases, coffee bags, produce). Never compare a per-pound price to a per-case price.

Credits: lines with negative Qty and Ext Price are vendor credits for shorts, damaged product and returns. Keep them in net spend.

Fees: FEE-FUEL is a fuel surcharge and FEE-DLVY a delivery fee. They are not products and have no Price File entry. Count them in spend, but leave them out of item price comparisons and rebate math.

CMSY: when the commissary sends prepped product to a hotel, the system books a transfer line under CMSY so usage shows up. The real purchase is already on a hotel's lines, so CMSY double counts. Always exclude CMSY from store spend. Store spend means Palm Key, Harborlight and Sandpiper.

Item codes: three products were re-coded by their vendors mid-period, same product, new number: CHICKEN BREAST BNLS SKLS 6 OZ (Bayfront Meats): BF1295 until 2025-08-24, then BF1842 from 2025-09-04; OIL FRYER CANOLA CLEAR (Coastline Provisions): CP10351 until 2025-09-21, then CP10883 from 2025-10-01; CREAM HEAVY 40% (Sunrise Dairy Co): SD3217 until 2025-12-25, then SD3769 from 2026-01-02. Treat each pair as one product.

Price File: the current item master with contract prices as of June 2026. Old codes and fee codes are not in it.

Contracts: Coastline Provisions is cost plus $2.10 per case with the fuel surcharge waived, 2% rebate, and the contract ends September 30, 2026; you are preparing the renewal. Bayfront Meats is fixed prices per the Price File from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026; the earlier 2024 Bayfront contract is not in the file. Gulf Breeze Produce renewed in January 2026, so it has two rows; use the one whose dates cover the invoice. Tidewater Seafood's contract ended February 28, 2026 and you have been month to month on the same terms since. Sunrise Dairy is written "Sunrise Dairy Co." with a period in the contracts file; it is the same vendor. Mangrove Coffee Roasters has no contract; you buy at list. Rebate % is in percent points (2.0 means 2%).

Rebates: paid quarterly by check, never on invoices, so they are not in Detail. The basis is net product spend at the hotels: credits netted, fees and CMSY excluded.

Problems you already know about: Bayfront billed the ribeye at $12.95 per pound in March and April 2026 against the $11.85 contract price. Coastline started adding a $14.75 fuel surcharge to its invoices in February 2026 even though the contract waives it. You have not filed claims yet. About 20 lines have an Ext Price that does not equal Qty x Unit Price; those are keying errors by the AP clerk when invoices were entered by hand, and the vendor's invoice is right at Qty x Unit Price.

The Summary tab is SUMIFS over Detail that you built for the monthly ops meeting. It includes CMSY and fees, so it overstates store spend.

Coastline is your biggest vendor, a bit under 40% of store spend.

Your goals: check every charge against the contract terms, find savings before the Coastline renewal, and get a clean spend view by hotel without CMSY.

You do not know exact totals offhand, hotel revenue or occupancy, or why any other price moved. Answer only what you are asked, briefly, like a busy purchasing manager. If a question is not covered here, say "not sure". Do not volunteer facts you were not asked about.

eval_questions.q: What was total store spend (the three hotels, net of credits, including fees) from Jan 2025 through Jun 2026?
eval_questions.a: $807,226.50. That is every Detail line except location CMSY (internal transfers), with credit lines netted in and fee lines included.

eval_questions.q: Which vendor gets the largest share of store spend, and what share is it?
eval_questions.a: Coastline Provisions, 38.4% of store spend ($310,206.17 of $807,226.50).

eval_questions.q: How many credit lines are in Detail and what do they total?
eval_questions.a: 198 credit lines (negative Qty and Ext Price, invoice numbers starting CM-) totaling -$14,781.53.

eval_questions.q: How much did the hotels pay in fees, split into fuel surcharges and delivery fees?
eval_questions.a: Fuel surcharges (FEE-FUEL) $2,884.00 on 335 lines; delivery fees (FEE-DLVY) $750.00 on 26 lines.

eval_questions.q: Did any vendor bill above its contract price while a fixed-price contract was in force? Which item, how many lines, which months, and how much in total?
eval_questions.a: Yes. Bayfront Meats: BEEF RIBEYE LIP ON 12 UP CH billed at $12.95 per LB against the $11.85 contract price on 9 store lines in 2026-03 and 2026-04, $233.06 over contract in total (211.87 lb).

eval_questions.a: OIL FRYER CANOLA CLEAR from Coastline Provisions, up 36.4%. Its item code changed mid-period, so grouping by Item # hides it; by code alone the top riser looks like PEPPER BELL GREEN (16.0%).

eval_questions.a: 20 lines; Ext Price minus Qty x Unit Price nets to $242.81 across them.

eval_questions.q: What was store spend by hotel in Q2 2026 (April to June), net of credits and including fees?
eval_questions.a: Palm Key $73,837.43; Harborlight $32,385.41; Sandpiper $26,447.69. CMSY is not a hotel and is left out.

eval_questions.q: What rebate should Coastline Provisions owe on calendar 2025 purchases?
eval_questions.a: $3,897.33: 2% of $194,866.29, Coastline net product spend at the hotels in 2025 (credits netted, fees and CMSY transfers excluded). Rebates arrive by check and are not in Detail.

eval_questions.a: 544 of 6000 lines (9.1%): 361 fee lines (FEE-FUEL, FEE-DLVY have no Price File entry) and 183 lines on the retired codes BF1295, CP10351, SD3217, which were replaced by new codes mid-period.
